conditions: Real u and v continuously differentiable on the same interval; du=u' dx and dv=v' dx for a shared real variable x. Indefinite integrals are interpreted up to an additive constant.
spoken_aliases: the integral of u d v equals u times v minus the integral of v d u
the integral of u with respect to v equals the product of u and v minus the integral of v with respect to u

evidence: The product rule gives d(uv)=u dv+v du. Rearrange and integrate on the interval. Differentiating the right-hand side recovers u v', so the two antiderivatives differ by at most a constant.
Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-2/pages/3-1-integration-by-parts. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
